issues.should_be: true — a truck (commercial vehicle) threw up the stone that cracked the windscreen, so a third party was involved even though its insurer/registration is not named
issues.evidence: Customer email received 2026-10-10: 'A stone thrown up by a truck on the motorway cracked my windscreen.' Handler playbook: 'When the other driver is a commercial vehicle (van, truck, lorry, delivery vehicle), refer the claim to a handler so Veridia can recover the money from their insurer.' The staged claim records third party involved = false and therefore skips this mandatory referral.

issues.should_be: false — the damage was caused by a stone projected by another vehicle, not by the policyholder; note this does not change the C3 outcome because the not-at-fault waiver in contract Article 5.2 applies only to C2, so the €50 C3 deductible and €430 payout are unaffected
issues.evidence: Customer email received 2026-10-10 ('A stone thrown up by a truck...'); Veridia contract Article 5.2 (not-at-fault waiver limited to C2) and Article 2 (C3 standard deductible €50).

verdict.summary: The claim is timely (reported 2026-10-10 for a 2026-10-09 incident, within the 5-day deadline of Article 4.1), C3 glass breakage is in the Policy Schedule, both required documents (photos, repair quote) were received, no exclusion applies, and the €430 payout (€480 − €50 C3 deductible, no assessor needed under Article 6.1) is arithmetically consistent — but the email clearly states a truck threw up the stone, so the recorded 'third party involved: false' and 'at fault: true' contradict the email and the playbook's mandatory referral to a handler for recovery from the truck's insurer.
